blocks.text: The Children's Internet Protection Act (CIPA) is aimed to prevent children from accessing obscene or harmful content over the internet. To learn more, refer to the Children's Internet Protection Act (CIPA). Schools or libraries are required to be CIPA compliant to receive discounts on internet access or internal connections through the E-rate program.

To aid schools and organizations to be compliant with the CIPA requirements, Zscaler provides a predefined URL filtering rule (CIPA Compliance Rule) and a control (Enable CIPA Compliance) to enable the predefined rule. It also provides a CIPA Compliance Report which gives insights into the traffic and users that are blocked from accessing the prohibited content based on the CIPA Compliance Rule.

blocks.item: Enabling CIPA Compliance

To activate the CIPA Compliance Rule, enable the Enable CIPA Compliance option from the Data Security > Inline CASB > Advanced Policy Settings. To learn more, see Configuring Advanced Policy Settings.
Effects of Enabling CIPA Compliance
Effects of Disabling CIPA Compliance
You cannot enable the Enable CIPA Compliance option when:
The number of URL filtering policy rules exceeds the limit.
A rule with rule order 1 exists with a higher admin rank.
The CIPA Compliance Rule is activated under Internet Access > Policy > URL Filtering.
The following Advanced URL Filtering Options under Data Security > Inline CASB > Advanced Policy Settings are enabled. You cannot disable the following options:
Enable Suspicious New Domains Lookup
Enable AI/ML-based Content Categorization
Enable Embedded Sites Categorization
Enforce SafeSearch
To learn more, see Configuring Advanced Policy Settings.
The CIPA Compliance Report option is enabled under the following locations:
Liability Exposure
From the navigation menu, go to Analytics > Reports > Interactive Reports.
On the Standard Reports tab, go to the Liability Exposure section to view the report.
Scheduled Reports
From the navigation menu, go to Analytics > Reports > Interactive Reports.
On the Scheduled Reports tab, click Add.
The Add Scheduled Report window appears.
In the Add Scheduled Report window, for Report, select CIPA Compliance Report, and configure the rest of the window.
Save and activate the change.
See image.
To learn more, see CIPA Compliance Report.

When you disable the Enable CIPA Compliance option, a warning message appears and we can add an image. You can get the image in beta; just disable the toggle in Advanced Settings and the warning appears.
The CIPA Compliance Rule gets disabled under Internet Access > Policy > URL Filtering. However, you can view the disabled rule.

The Advanced URL Filtering Options under the Data Security > Inline CASB > Advanced Policy Settings are set to the recommended policy settings. To learn more, see Recommended URL & Cloud App Control Policy.
Viewing CIPA Compliance Rule
You can view the CIPA Compliance Rule under Internet Access > Policy > URL Filtering if you select the Enable CIPA Compliance option at least once. To learn more, see Enabling CIPA Compliance.
You can delete the CIPA Compliance Rule only when you disable the Enable CIPA Compliance toggle.
The attributes defined for the rule are as follows:

table: (Editable) Order of precedence of the rule. When the CIPA Compliance Rule is activated for the first time, it takes the highest precedence (rule order 1) by default. The rule order is automatically incremented by 1 for the other rules. You can edit the rule order based on your preference.
(Editable) Admin rank of the logged-in user. If the logged-in user does not have an admin rank, then the rule is created with an admin rank 7.
(Non-editable) Name of the rule. You cannot create any custom URL filtering rule with the name CIPA Compliance Rule.

Adult Sex Education, Adult Themes, Alcohol/Tobacco, Anonymizer, Computer Hacking, Copyright Infringement, Drugs, Gambling, K-12 Sex Education, Lingerie/Bikini, Mature Humor, Militancy/Hate and Extremism, Newly Registered and Observed Domains, Nudity, Other Adult Material, Other Illegal or Questionable, Pornography, Profanity, Questionable, Body Art, Social Networking Adult, Tasteless, Violence, Weapons/Bombs

(Non-editable) List of all the predefined categories under the URL super category, Legal Liabilities with predefined URLs and keywords. The custom categories under Legal Liabilities are excluded. You cannot add or delete URL categories from the predefined list. However, you can add or delete custom URLs and keywords (CIPA related) from any predefined category under Legal Liabilities.
OPTIONS, GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, TRACE, CONNECT, OTHER, ALL
(Non-editable) Applicable to all the users in the organization.
(Non-editable) Applicable to all the groups in the organization.
(Non-editable) Applicable to all the departments in the organization.
(Non-editable) Applicable to all the locations of the organization.
(Non-editable) Applicable to all the location groups of the organization.
(Non-editable) Access is denied to all the sites that fall under the specified URL categories.
(Non-editable) No exception is allowed for the blocked sites.
(Editable) Additional notes or information about the rule.
